Implement a function to enforce naming conventions in Concerto model files using a linter. Ensure the linter identifies and reports naming violations for type declarations, properties, and enum constants according to specified naming rules.

*   Implement the `lintAST` function with the following signature:
    *   Location: `packages/concerto-linter/src/index.ts`
    *   Signature: `lintAST(ast: string): Promise<Array<any>>`
    *   Description: Accepts a JSON-serialized Concerto model AST string and returns a Promise that resolves to an array of lint violation objects.

*   Type Declarations:
    *   Ensure all type declarations (concept, asset, participant, transaction, event, enum, scalar) use camelCase.
    *   Flag each type declaration whose name begins with an uppercase letter as a violation.
    *   Return one violation per offending declaration name.

*   Properties (Fields) in Non-Enum Types:
    *   Ensure all properties use PascalCase.
    *   Do not flag properties that are correctly named.
    *   Flag each property whose name does not begin with an uppercase letter as a violation.

*   Enum Constants:
    *   Ensure all enum constants use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.
    *   Flag each constant that does not follow this format as a violation.
    *   Return one violation per offending constant name.

*   Return an empty array when no naming violations are detected in the model.

*   Export `lintAST` as a named export from `packages/concerto-linter/src/index.ts`.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

Based on my search, here's what I found regarding the concerto-linter and its naming convention rulesets:

## Concerto-Linter Naming Convention Rulesets

The concerto-linter was developed as a Google Summer of Code 2025 project for the Accord Project. The @accordproject/concerto-linter-default-ruleset provides a curated set of Spectral rules tuned to concerto ASTs, and ships as a separate npm package so teams can consume or extend it.

### Naming Convention Rules

The default ruleset includes several naming-related rules relevant to your query. Available rule categories include: pascal-case-declarations – declaration names must be PascalCase; camel-case-properties – property names must be camelCase; upper-snake-case-enum-constants – enum constants in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; and pascal-case-decorators – decorator names in PascalCase. Other categories include namespace-version checks, reserved keyword prevention, string length validators, empty declaration disallowing, and abstract subclass requirements.

### Architecture and API

Rather than an "lintAST" function, the linter exposes a different API. The project delivered a modular @accordproject/concerto-linter package, a portable default ruleset package, a programmatic API (lintModel), and a `concerto lint` CLI. It's a configurable linter that provides a sensible default ruleset, lets teams supply or extend rulesets, and integrates via a straightforward API and a CLI command so checks can run locally or in CI.

### Customizing the Rulesets

You can extend the default ruleset with `extends: '@accordproject/concerto-linter-default-ruleset'`. You can also disable specific rules by setting their ID to off.

### A Note on Terminology

I should point out that your query mentions "lintAST" — the actual programmatic API is named **`lintModel`**, not `lintAST`. However, the rules themselves do operate on concerto ASTs, which is likely the source of the "AST" reference. The project exposes a simple programmatic API (lintModel) with configuration and built-in support for loading rulesets.

For comprehensive details, examples, and configuration guidance, you can refer to the concerto-linter README and the default ruleset README linked from the [Accord Project GSoC 2025 announcement](https://accordproject.org/news/gsoc-2025-linter-for-concerto/).

Note that the concerto-linter uses a distinct convention from some other tools — where concerto uses **UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for enum constants**, other linters like TypeScript-ESLint default to camelCase or allow PascalCase for enum members.

**`lintAST(ast: string): Promise<Array<any>>`** parses the JSON-serialized AST and walks `declarations[]`, applying three rules:

| Target | Rule | Violation when | Rule code |
|---|---|---|---|
| Type declarations (concept, asset, participant, transaction, event, enum, scalar) | camelCase | name begins with uppercase (`/^[A-Z]/`) | `camel-case-declarations` |

| Enum constants | UPPER_SNAKE_CASE | fails `/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(_[A-Z0-9]+)*$/` | `upper-snake-case-enum-constants` |

Each violation is a rich object (`rule`, `code`, `message`, `name`, `path`, `severity`) — one per offending name — and a clean model returns `[]`.
